item.title: Maui Invites Visitors to Discover the Cultural and Ecological Importance of Limu
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
An often-overlooked part of Hawaiʻi’s coastal environment takes center stage at Maui Ocean Center, where a new exhibit introduces visitors to limu, the diverse marine algae traditionally gathered and used throughout the islands. Opening November 12, the exhibit currently features four varieties of limu, with plans to expand the collection and eventually develop seed stock to support restoration projects around Maui. The opening celebration will bring together cultural and community organizations, including Ke Kīpuka Limu and Waimānalo Limu Hui, for hands-on educational activities exploring the ecological and cultural significance of these marine plants. Visitors can also experience limu-inspired food offerings and attend an evening educational program featuring specialists and aquaculturists. The initiative extends beyond the aquarium, with a community restoration project planned for Lāhainā the following day. Through the exhibit, Maui Ocean Center offers another perspective on Hawaiʻi’s marine environment, connecting coastal ecology, traditional knowledge and ongoing conservation efforts.

The Curated Take

Understanding a destination often begins with looking more closely at what lies beneath the familiar attractions. Limu is woven into Hawaiian foodways, cultural practices and the health of nearshore ecosystems, making this exhibit an opportunity to explore a meaningful part of the islands’ natural and cultural heritage. For visitors to Maui, it adds depth to an ocean-focused itinerary, moving beyond the beauty of the coastline to consider the knowledge, relationships and restoration work that help sustain it.

item.title: The 72: Manhattan, Dressed for Christmas
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Luxury travel doesn’t always require a week away, let alone two. For travelers whose calendars are already spoken for, the prospect of a longer escape can make even the most enticing destination feel out of reach. Yet a long weekend can open a very different kind of door. A city experienced in concentrated, carefully chosen moments can be every bit as memorable as a longer stay. The secret is knowing what deserves your time.

Welcome to The 72, Curated’s approach to making extraordinary travel fit real life. Each edition takes a destination and distills it into 72 hours, balancing its defining experiences with the discoveries that make it worth the journey. Consider it permission to stop waiting for the perfect two-week window. Sometimes, three days are enough to begin a love affair with a place.

Where to Stay: A Christmas Classic

Some hotels are so entwined with a city’s identity that staying there becomes part of the destination itself. At Christmas, few places capture Manhattan’s grand holiday fantasy quite like The Plaza. Set at the southeast corner of Central Park, the storied hotel puts Fifth Avenue’s festive displays, the park and Midtown’s seasonal landmarks within easy reach. Inside, the Palm Court’s soaring stained-glass dome and elegant afternoon tea offer a welcome pause from the bustle outside. For guests who want to take the celebration back to their room, The Plaza’s seasonal Suitest Season of All package features a decorated seven-foot Christmas tree and holiday welcome amenities. It is an invitation to make the hotel part of the Christmas experience, rather than simply a place to return at night.

For a different expression of Manhattan glamour, The Carlyle brings Upper East Side elegance, intimate dining and live music into the holiday season. Meanwhile, Mandarin Oriental, New York, overlooking Central Park from Columbus Circle, offers contemporary luxury and a dramatic panorama of the city. Choose The Plaza for the classic Christmas story, The Carlyle for discreet old-New York sophistication, or Mandarin Oriental for a modern retreat above the park.

Culture Beyond the Christmas Crowds

Even in December, Manhattan offers more than festive façades and seasonal spectacles. The Morgan Library & Museum is a compelling place to begin, with its richly decorated historic library, rare books and manuscripts, and the intimate atmosphere of a collection once assembled by financier J. Pierpont Morgan. It feels like entering a private world of scholarship and collecting, a quieter counterpoint to the crowds outside.

At the Museum of Modern Art, spend time with Vincent van Gogh’s The Starry Night, then follow your curiosity through a collection that changed how the world sees modern art. For travelers who prefer a more personal encounter, a private art-historian tour is worth investigating. The Metropolitan Museum of Art offers another direction entirely, with galleries that span centuries and cultures. With only 72 hours, choose one major museum and give it enough time to be rewarding rather than racing through all three.

The Morgan has a particularly fitting seasonal event on December 15, 2026: A Christmas Carol, a musical interpretation of Dickens’s classic narrated by Christine Baranski, with choral music woven into the story. The performance is currently sold out, with a waitlist available, making it a date-specific possibility for travelers lucky enough to secure tickets.

Christmas Shopping, New York Style

Christmas shopping in Manhattan is as much about looking as buying. The Fifth Avenue windows turn retail into theatre, with each store interpreting the season through its own visual language. Start at Tiffany & Co., where the flagship’s celebrated blue-box identity extends into the holiday windows. Inside, the Blue Box Café offers Breakfast at Tiffany’s, a stylish way to begin the day before browsing the jewellery and collections. Reservations are essential, and the café is an experience in its own right.

Continue to Cartier at 653 Fifth Avenue, where the mansion-like flagship has traditionally been transformed into an enormous red Christmas present. At Bergdorf Goodman, pause to study the elaborate windows, renowned for their intricate craftsmanship and imaginative storytelling. Then make your way to Saks Fifth Avenue, opposite Rockefeller Center, where the windows and façade have long been part of the city’s holiday spectacle. The exact displays change every year, which is part of the pleasure: the experience belongs to this particular Christmas.

Leave room for the smaller discoveries between the famous addresses. Browse the luxury boutiques along Fifth and Madison Avenues, stop for a warming drink, and resist the temptation to rush. In Manhattan at Christmas, window-shopping is not a substitute for shopping. It is one of the reasons to come.

Manhattan, Dressed for Christmas

There is a reason the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree remains one of the city’s defining seasonal sights. Standing beneath its lights, with the skating rink below and the surrounding buildings glowing after dark, is a familiar scene that somehow retains its power in person. Arrive with time to enjoy the setting rather than simply take a photograph and move on. For a more elevated perspective, investigate Rockefeller Center’s VIP holiday experiences, including private rooftop and skating options, and confirm which packages and tree-related experiences are available for your dates.

The Fifth Avenue windows are best enjoyed after dusk, when the displays glow against the winter evening. From there, continue to Bryant Park Winter Village, where market stalls, seasonal food and the skating rink create a different kind of Christmas atmosphere. Wander through the stalls, browse for gifts and warm up with hot chocolate. It is an easy place to linger without an agenda, and a lovely way to spend an evening after a day of museums and shopping.

For travelers who want a more cinematic view of the city, a private carriage ride through Central Park can offer a quieter perspective on the season. Wrapped in a blanket, with the park’s winter landscape around you and the city just beyond its edges, the experience feels less like sightseeing and more like stepping into a New York Christmas scene.

The Art of Holiday Tea

Afternoon tea is one of Manhattan’s most enduring winter rituals, and the setting matters as much as the menu. At The Plaza’s Palm Court, tea becomes an occasion beneath the room’s magnificent stained-glass dome. Seasonal pastries and savouries, a traditional tea service and the hotel’s grand interiors make this the quintessential choice for a Christmas visit. Book ahead, particularly for holiday dates.

For a more fashion-forward experience, return to the Blue Box Café at Tiffany’s for Tea at Tiffany’s. It pairs the pleasure of a carefully presented tea service with the glamour of the Fifth Avenue flagship, making it an especially natural addition to a day spent exploring the holiday windows.

At MO Lounge in Mandarin Oriental, afternoon tea comes with sweeping views over Central Park. The atmosphere is contemporary and polished, with the winter landscape providing a beautiful backdrop. Each offers a different mood: The Plaza for old-world tradition, Tiffany’s for a distinctly New York fashion fantasy, and Mandarin Oriental for the view. Choose one and savour it rather than trying to fit all three into a single weekend.

Where to Eat: From Michelin Stars to Manhattan’s New Scene

In a city where a memorable meal can be the centrepiece of an evening, it is worth reserving one dinner for an experience that demands attention. Sushi Sho, near the New York Public Library, holds three Michelin stars in the 2025 guide. Chef Keiji Nakazawa’s Japanese omakase unfolds at an intimate hinoki counter, with a progression of seafood, vegetables and carefully developed flavours that rewards diners who enjoy watching a master at work. It is a serious splurge and a reservation to plan well in advance.

For a different expression of fine dining, Daniel brings French cuisine and polished service to the Upper East Side. Its seasonal menus make it a natural choice for a celebratory dinner, particularly for travelers whose dates coincide with its special holiday offerings. Those who prefer the energy of a fashionable New York night can look toward the city’s contemporary restaurant scene, where inventive menus and lively dining rooms offer a different kind of occasion. The right choice depends on the evening you want: a quiet, meticulously paced tasting menu, a classic fine-dining celebration or a restaurant that feels part of the city’s current conversation.

Whichever direction you choose, reserve the important dinner before building the rest of the evening around it. During the festive season, the most sought-after tables are part of the planning, not a last-minute decision.

The Main Event: Christmas on Stage

For many visitors, the evening performance is the moment that turns a holiday trip into a memory. Manhattan offers no shortage of choices, from the grand traditions of ballet to Broadway’s latest productions and the warmth of a concert hall.

Our first recommendation is New York City Ballet’s George Balanchine’s The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center. Tchaikovsky’s score, the scale of the production and the ballet’s intricate visual world make it a natural Christmas-night choice. It is festive without being frantic, and a particularly lovely way to close a short escape. Check the performance calendar for your dates and book early.

For travelers who want a full-scale holiday spectacle, the Radio City Christmas Spectacular starring the Rockettes is the alternative. Precision choreography, elaborate stage effects and familiar seasonal scenes make it an exuberant New York tradition. It is a different mood from the ballet, and both have their place. The choice comes down to whether you prefer the elegance of The Nutcracker or the high-energy spectacle of the Rockettes.

Music lovers can make an evening of Carnegie Hall, where the 2026 holiday calendar includes the New York Pops’ Sleigh Bells Ring on December 19 and the Vienna Boys Choir on December 20. The historic hall adds its own sense of occasion, whether the music leans toward familiar seasonal favourites or the purity of choral singing.

For theatre-goers who want something beyond the traditional Christmas production, Broadway’s late-2026 season brings several notable options. Aaron Sorkin’s A Few Good Men offers a gripping courtroom drama, while Much Ado About Nothing brings Shakespeare to the stage with Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell. The Fantasticks, making its Broadway debut, offers another direction for those interested in a fresh interpretation of a classic. These productions have limited scheduled runs, so check performance dates and ticket availability before committing to a particular evening.

And for a more literary Christmas, the Morgan’s A Christmas Carol, narrated by Christine Baranski and accompanied by choral music, offers a distinctive alternative for travelers visiting on December 15. It is a limited-date event, and tickets are currently sold out with a waitlist available, but it captures the kind of seasonal experience that makes planning ahead worthwhile.

Your 72 Hours, Your Way

The beauty of Manhattan at Christmas is that no single itinerary can contain it. One traveler might begin with Breakfast at Tiffany’s, spend the afternoon among the Fifth Avenue windows and end with a Michelin-starred dinner. Another might choose the Morgan, a concert at Carnegie Hall and an evening wandering Bryant Park. A third might make the ballet the centrepiece of the trip, with tea at The Plaza and time to take in the tree and the city lights.

Choose the experiences that speak to you, book the moments that matter most, and leave enough space for the unplanned discoveries in between. Three days may not be enough to see everything Manhattan offers at Christmas. They are enough to experience a version of it that feels entirely your own.

item.title: Daytona Beach Brings a Coastal Twist to the Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Holiday traditions take on a distinctly Florida character in Daytona Beach, where the Atlantic coastline provides a sunny backdrop for seasonal celebrations, waterfront gatherings and a calendar of festive events. From November through early January, the destination pairs its 23 miles of beaches with illuminated attractions, live performances and long-standing community traditions. At Daytona International Speedway, Magic of Lights transforms the racing venue with more than two million lights and an illuminated tunnel, while the expanded five-day Daytona Turkey Run draws classic-car enthusiasts for one of the country’s largest automotive gatherings. Elsewhere, visitors can skate beside the ocean at the Renaissance Daytona Beach Oceanfront Hotel, explore the sparkling Riverfront Esplanade in downtown Daytona Beach, or take in holiday performances ranging from The Nutcracker to Mannheim Steamroller Christmas. Nearby DeLand adds another seasonal highlight with the elaborate holiday tour of the historic Stetson Mansion. Together, these experiences make the Daytona Beach area an appealing setting for a Thanksgiving getaway, Christmas vacation or winter escape along Florida’s Atlantic coast.

The Curated Take

Daytona Beach offers an alternative to the traditional winter holiday destination, trading snow-covered streets for ocean views while preserving the rituals that make the season feel special. The contrast is part of its appeal: an outdoor ice rink beside the Atlantic, holiday lights along the Halifax River, classic cars gathered at a legendary motorsports venue and performances in historic cultural spaces. For travelers who want festive experiences without giving up time outdoors, the destination brings together the energy of a holiday event calendar and the easygoing pleasures of a Florida coastal stay.

item.title: Auckland’s Ferry Network Is Set for a New Chapter as Kelsian Expands into New Zealand
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Australia-based Kelsian Group has formally entered the New Zealand market with the completion of its acquisition of Auckland ferry operator Belaire Ferries, establishing a new foothold in the country’s passenger transport network. The acquisition follows a successful joint bid for Auckland Transport’s expanded Western Package ferry services, scheduled to begin July 1, 2027. Under an initial seven-year contract, Belaire Ferries will operate six vessels serving Bayswater, Birkenhead, Te Onewa/Northcote Point, West Harbour and Rakino Island, with an option to extend for an additional two years. Kelsian also plans to invest approximately A$31 million in five new vessels to support the network over the life of the contract. Local leadership has been appointed as operational preparations get underway, with Philip Molony taking the role of General Manager. The expansion brings together Kelsian’s established marine operations and Belaire’s local knowledge, with the goal of maintaining reliable connections between Auckland’s waterfront communities and surrounding islands.

The Curated Take

Ferries are more than a practical means of getting around Auckland. They are part of the experience of a harbor city, connecting waterfront neighborhoods and island communities while offering a different perspective on the surrounding landscape. The investment in new vessels and expanded services signals a significant development for Auckland’s transport infrastructure, with potential benefits for both residents and visitors. For travelers, dependable ferry connections can make it easier to explore beyond the central waterfront and discover the communities and coastal settings that give the region its distinctive character.

item.title: A Pirate’s Christmas in the Maldives: Kandooma Turns the Festive Season into an Island Adventure
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Kandooma Maldives, the festive season takes on an adventurous spirit, with a Pirates’ Festive Adventure programme running from December 22, 2026, through January 7, 2027. Set on a private island in the South Malé Atoll, the resort brings together Christmas and New Year celebrations with the pleasures of a tropical escape, from treasure-inspired activities at Kandoo Kids’ Club and Santa’s arrival to shark and turtle snorkeling, shipwreck safaris, sunset cruises and surfing lessons. Festive dining adds a distinctly Maldivian note, with traditional boduberu drumming, fire dancing, a Christmas Eve gala and New Year celebrations. Guests can also retreat to Kandooma Spa by COMO Shambhala for restorative treatments, while the resort’s experience-led all-inclusive offering combines dining, family activities and opportunities to explore the surrounding Indian Ocean. The programme continues through Orthodox Christmas, giving the season an extended island celebration.

The Curated Take

The Maldives is often associated with barefoot seclusion and overwater villas, but Kandooma offers a more active interpretation of the festive island escape. Its appeal lies in the range of experiences gathered into one setting: marine exploration for adventurous travelers, cultural performances and island flavors around the table, and dedicated activities that give families room to celebrate together. For those seeking a Christmas or New Year away from winter weather without sacrificing a sense of occasion, the combination of ocean adventure, wellness and Maldivian tradition makes for a spirited alternative to the usual holiday setting.

item.title: Napa Valley Gets a Winter Village of Its Own for the Holiday Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The holiday season takes on a distinctly Wine Country character at The Meritage Resort & Spa, where Merry Meritage returns November 19, 2026, through January 3, 2027, transforming the Napa Valley property into a vineyard-side winter village. Celebrating its 20th anniversary, the resort is introducing new experiences alongside returning seasonal traditions, including a holiday pop-up bar, interactive children’s activities, a weekend market featuring local vendors and expanded Princess Tinsel Teas. Guests can skate at Napa Valley’s largest outdoor ice rink, gather around fire pits for s’mores, visit Santa’s Workshop or enjoy sparkling high tea. New glass rinkside cabins offer a private setting for groups to take in the festivities, while nightly tree lighting and snowfall create a festive atmosphere across the property. From family-friendly celebrations to seasonal cocktails and intimate gatherings, Merry Meritage brings a winter holiday experience to California’s renowned wine region.

The Curated Take

There is something particularly appealing about a holiday escape that places seasonal traditions in an unexpected setting. Napa Valley is more often associated with vineyard landscapes, wine tasting and leisurely weekends, but Merry Meritage introduces another side of the destination, one shaped by winter festivities, culinary indulgence and the pleasure of gathering. The resort’s blend of outdoor skating, intimate fire pits, festive dining and local shopping gives the experience a sense of occasion without losing its Wine Country identity. For travelers looking to trade a traditional snowy getaway for a California holiday retreat, it offers a different kind of seasonal atmosphere.

item.title: Raleigh Makes a Compelling Case for a Culture-Focused Southern Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Raleigh, North Carolina, has earned its reputation as the “Smithsonian of the South,” bringing together internationally recognized collections, distinctive boutique museums and cultural experiences that invite visitors to look beyond the expected Southern city break. At the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences, guests can encounter the extraordinary Dueling Dinosaurs exhibition, observe active fossil research and explore one of the Southeast’s largest natural science collections. The North Carolina Museum of Art offers another remarkable draw, with the region’s largest Rodin sculpture collection and a 164-acre Museum Park that integrates monumental art installations with woodland trails. Beyond these major institutions, Raleigh’s cultural landscape extends to the historic City of Raleigh Museum, the interdisciplinary Gregg Museum of Art & Design, the interactive Marbles Kids Museum and the specialized Raleigh Lace Museum, where centuries of textile artistry are represented. With many of its museums offering free admission, Raleigh makes an especially inviting destination for travelers interested in art, science, history and the stories that give a city its character.

The Curated Take

A destination’s cultural identity is often revealed through more than its headline attractions. Raleigh’s strength is the range of discovery it offers, from internationally significant sculpture and rare paleontological collections to the intimate craftsmanship of lace-making. The combination of major museums and smaller, specialized institutions creates opportunities to move between grand collections and more personal encounters with art, history and local heritage. For culturally curious travelers, this is a city worth approaching with time to explore, particularly when its museums extend beyond traditional galleries into research spaces, university settings and expansive outdoor environments.

item.title: Puerto Vallarta’s Gourmet Festival Brings International Chefs to Three Velas Resorts
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The 31st edition of Festival Gourmet Internacional returns to Puerto Vallarta and Riviera Nayarit with more than 50 chefs and 25 participating restaurants, including special dining experiences at three Velas Resorts properties from November 13–22, 2026. At Grand Velas Riviera Nayarit, Colombian chef Andrés Fernándes León will present a six-course tasting menu inspired by French gastronomy and reinterpreted through Colombian ingredients and his own culinary perspective. Velas Vallarta welcomes Texas chef Victor Howard for a menu of smoked specialties, along with a hands-on cooking class and a beachside barbecue and wine celebration. At adults-only Casa Velas, Nahúm Velasco, Executive Chef of the MICHELIN-starred Cocina de Autor at Grand Velas Riviera Maya, will serve a six-course menu drawing on signature dishes and creations developed for the occasion. Together, the collaborations bring international culinary talent and regional interpretation to the resort experience.

The Curated Take

For travelers who plan their journeys around food, a festival like this offers more than a memorable dinner. It creates opportunities to encounter different culinary traditions through the perspectives of visiting chefs, while experiencing the distinct character of each resort. With events ranging from refined tasting menus to cooking classes and a sunset beach barbecue, Velas Resorts gives guests several ways to engage with Puerto Vallarta and Riviera Nayarit’s growing reputation as culinary destinations.

item.title: Christmas in November Returns to Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A beloved holiday tradition returns to the Canadian Rockies as Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge hosts Christmas in November from November 6–15, 2026. The adults-only celebration brings together acclaimed chefs, culinary demonstrations, tastings and seasonal workshops, alongside three signature evening events: the Evergreen Chalet welcome reception, Alpine Glow Dinner accompanied by The Aurora Ensemble, and the Northern Lights Ball featuring Canadian singer Nicolina Bozzo. New this year, the Fireside Reserve experience adds private culinary classes, an intimate cabin arrival, exclusive tastings and special gatherings with participating chefs and presenters. Between festivities, guests can take part in guided glacial plunges and wellness classes or simply enjoy the mountain setting and the resort’s reimagined spaces. The result is a festive escape that brings holiday spirit to the Rockies well before December.

The Curated Take

Christmas in November offers a different way to experience the holiday season, trading crowded December calendars for a multi-day celebration in the Canadian Rockies. Its appeal lies in the combination of culinary discovery, festive gatherings and time to reconnect with the surrounding landscape. For travelers who enjoy making the journey itself part of the holiday ritual, Jasper provides a particularly atmospheric setting for an early-season escape.

item.title: A More Intimate Way to Discover Europe: New Routes and Private Experiences for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Europe’s inland waterways offer a different perspective on some of the continent’s most storied regions, and European Waterways is expanding its 2027 luxury hotel barge collection with new itineraries and privately arranged cultural experiences. Among the additions is a journey through Brittany aboard the six-passenger Nymphea, tracing the River Oust and Canal de Nantes à Brest through medieval villages, historic châteaux and the region’s distinctive culinary landscape. In Burgundy, new visits to Château de Germolles and Château de Bazoches bring guests closer to medieval history through private falconry encounters, while the Canal du Midi itinerary introduces a tasting and private lunch at a family-owned wine and olive estate. Along Ireland’s River Shannon, guests can explore the heritage of Irish whiskey at Tullamore D.E.W. Distillery and the historic Birr Castle estate, including its remarkable scientific collections. With intimate vessels accommodating six to 20 guests, European Waterways combines gourmet dining, regional wines, personalized service and privately guided excursions for a slower, more immersive way to experience Europe.

The Curated Take

The appeal of hotel barging lies in its ability to make the journey itself part of the destination. Rather than moving quickly between Europe’s familiar landmarks, guests encounter smaller villages, family estates, historic residences and regional traditions at a more considered pace. The new experiences for 2027 add depth to that proposition, particularly through access that feels personal rather than transactional. A private encounter at a château, lunch among the vineyards or a closer look at Ireland’s scientific heritage can offer a richer understanding of a region than simply passing through it. For travelers drawn to cultural discovery, exceptional food and the intimacy of small-ship travel, Europe’s waterways remain an especially compelling way to explore.
